title: Planning a Working Break in Corbett: Check Connectivity Before You Commit
seoTitle: Corbett Workation Planning | Connectivity and Room Checks
description: Evaluate a Corbett working break with specific questions about room connectivity, calls, workspace, power arrangements and the time you want off.

blocks.text: A working break needs more preparation than a normal holiday because your room must support a task as well as a stay. If you have calls, deadlines or a team depending on you, the word Wi-Fi in a facilities list is not enough to establish that the arrangement suits your work.
Treat Corbett as a place to visit with a clearly defined work requirement. Ask detailed questions before booking, and decide which commitments can reasonably be moved or completed before travel.
Describe the work you need to do
Different tasks have different requirements. Occasional email is not the same as several hours of video meetings, a large upload or a time-sensitive presentation.

Tell the resort the room category you are considering, the hours involved and the practical setup you need. Avoid assuming that a conference facility means every guest room has the same connectivity or workspace arrangement.
Ask about the actual room setup
Use specific questions and obtain current answers. A service available in a shared area may not be suitable for confidential or uninterrupted work.

items: What connectivity is available in the proposed room area?
Can the team discuss current performance and any limitations?
Is there suitable seating and a surface for the intended work?
What power arrangements apply, and what happens during an interruption?
Are quieter room requests possible, and what can be confirmed?

blocks.text: These are checks to make, not claims that a particular speed, backup supply or workspace is provided.
Keep critical work independent of the holiday

Consider completing major uploads and presentations before departure. Keep appropriate offline copies of the material you will need and follow your organisation's requirements for handling work information.

If uninterrupted connectivity is essential, do not rely on a leisure booking until you have established a suitable arrangement. A personal fallback should also be checked for actual coverage and suitability rather than assumed from a provider's general map.
Set boundaries with the people travelling
Explain which hours you intend to work and when you will be available for the holiday. A companion should not discover on arrival that every afternoon is committed to calls.

Keep the shared programme modest. Our [three-night itinerary](/blogs/three-night-corbett-itinerary) provides room for a slower pace, but it should not be read as an assurance that work can fit into any gap. The stay remains more enjoyable when work hours are explicit.
Distinguish a personal working break from a company offsite

A room-based stay and a group meeting need different arrangements. If several colleagues require sessions, equipment or a shared programme, use the [corporate offsite page](/corporate-offsites) rather than trying to assemble those requirements from individual room bookings.

For an individual visit, compare [accommodation](/accommodation) and review the [resort booking checklist](/blogs/resort-stay-checklist-corbett). Share the essential work requirements with the team before confirming. The right decision may be a suitable working break or a holiday taken after the deadline; clarity makes either choice better.

title: A Two-Day Corporate Offsite Agenda for Corbett
seoTitle: Two-Day Corporate Offsite Agenda in Corbett | Sample Plan
description: Build an overnight Corbett offsite around one clear outcome, focused sessions, useful breaks and an accountable closing discussion.

blocks.text: A two-day offsite should create a result that is harder to achieve in an ordinary office meeting. That might be agreeing priorities, resolving a cross-team issue or preparing a plan for the next quarter. Decide the outcome before choosing activities or filling the agenda.
For an overnight Corbett programme, the travel schedule also matters. A full workshop cannot begin effectively while half the group is still arriving or waiting to settle into rooms.
Start with a decision the group needs to make

Write one sentence describing what should be different at departure. For example, the team may need a prioritised action list with owners and dates. That is more useful than a broad goal such as improve alignment.
Ask participants to read a short briefing before the trip. Keep background presentations out of the main session where they would consume the time intended for discussion.
Use a programme with a clear progression

blocks.caption: Use a programme with a clear progression

blocks.text: This is an example, not a fixed resort package. The confirmed rooms, meeting arrangements and travel plan should determine the actual timetable.
Give each session an owner

Nominate a facilitator and a person recording decisions. Explain whether a session is intended to gather ideas, choose an option or approve an action. Confusing these purposes often makes a programme run late.

Leave enough time between sessions to reset the room and allow people a real break. If participants need to complete urgent work, identify a suitable period rather than letting calls interrupt every discussion.
Make the evening optional in the right way
A shared dinner can be valuable without requiring a highly produced activity. If you add an organised programme, consider the group's preferences and confirm the provider, duration and requirements.

Read the [team-building guide](/blogs/team-building-activities-corbett) before selecting something that only part of the team can comfortably join. Time together should support the purpose of the offsite rather than become a test of physical enthusiasm.
Close with accountability
At the final session, agree what was decided, who owns each action and when progress will be reviewed. Circulate a concise record while the discussion is still fresh.

Use the [offsite measurement guide](/blogs/offsite-success-measurement-corbett) to plan follow-up before the group travels home. A good closing discussion is easier when the desired outcome was clear at the beginning.

Discuss [corporate offsites at Corbett The Grand](/corporate-offsites) with your participant count, room requirements and meeting format. The venue should support the agenda, while the agenda should justify bringing the team together.

title: Building a Corporate Offsite Budget for Corbett
seoTitle: Corporate Offsite Budget in Corbett | Proposal Checklist
description: Compare group accommodation, meeting space, catering, transport and activities using a clear Corbett offsite budget with matching assumptions.

blocks.text: A corporate offsite quotation is easier to assess when the budget separates accommodation, meeting requirements and the group programme. A total per participant can be useful at the end, but it hides too much when different suppliers are working from different assumptions.
Prepare a brief before requesting proposals. Include dates, participant count, nights, rooming preferences, the purpose of the meeting and any essential equipment.
Separate fixed and headcount-dependent items
Some items may depend mainly on the meeting arrangement, while others change with the number of rooms or meals. Ask the provider to explain the basis of each charge.

blocks.caption: Separate fixed and headcount-dependent items

blocks.text: Add applicable taxes and any separately arranged services when calculating the complete proposal. This framework does not represent current resort pricing.
Calculate the accommodation accurately

Use the confirmed rooming approach rather than dividing the participant count by two automatically. Colleagues may need separate rooms or specific arrangements that the available categories do not provide.

For illustration, 12 rooms for two nights represents 24 room nights. That calculation does not decide how many colleagues can appropriately share. Confirm the [room categories](/accommodation) and sleeping arrangements with the team before applying a cost model.
Match meals to the actual programme
List arrivals, refreshments, lunches, dinners and departure breakfasts. Participants joining only the meeting may affect catering without affecting room nights.

Review the [two-day agenda](/blogs/two-day-corporate-offsite-agenda-corbett) alongside the budget. If a session needs an early setup or a late finish, identify any consequences for room access, staffing, catering or transport before approving the programme.
Make technical requirements explicit
A conference facility does not mean every item needed for your meeting is included. Specify presentation equipment, audio requirements, connectivity needs and the support you expect.

Use the [conference setup checklist](/blogs/conference-setup-checklist-corbett) to prepare the request. Ask suppliers to identify alternatives if an essential requirement cannot be met. Avoid buying an activity-heavy package that leaves the actual meeting under-specified.
Compare like-for-like proposals
Keep dates, headcount, rooming, meals and session requirements consistent. Mark optional items separately and agree who can approve changes.

Set a confirmation process for headcount, room allocations and added services. Understand payment, amendments and cancellation conditions before making a commitment. A lower total may reflect different inclusions rather than a more economical version of the same programme.

Send your brief through the [corporate enquiry page](/corporate-offsites). After the event, compare actual spend with the agreed scope and review outcomes using the [offsite success guide](/blogs/offsite-success-measurement-corbett). The budget should support a useful business gathering, not just the lowest headline rate.

title: Choosing Team-Building Activities for a Corbett Offsite
seoTitle: Team-Building Activities in Corbett | Offsite Planning
description: Select Corbett offsite activities according to the team's objective, participation needs, time available and the arrangements actually confirmed.

blocks.text: An offsite activity should help the team spend time together in a way that suits the people attending. It does not have to be physically demanding or heavily produced to be useful. A well-facilitated conversation can achieve more than an activity chosen only because it looks impressive in a proposal.
Start with the purpose of the offsite. A new team getting to know one another needs a different programme from a leadership group working through a difficult decision.
Choose the outcome before the activity

Ask what the activity should make possible: conversation across departments, collaborative problem-solving or a relaxed break after a demanding session. Then choose a format that supports that purpose.

blocks.caption: Choose the outcome before the activity

blocks.text: These are programme ideas, not a list of activities automatically provided by the resort.
Make participation workable

Consider mobility, confidence, language and personal preferences before choosing a group activity. Ask participants about practical needs through an appropriate channel and avoid making someone explain a private issue in front of colleagues.

Offer a meaningful alternative where an activity does not suit everyone. Optional participation works best when the alternative is clearly acceptable, rather than making a guest feel they are letting the team down.
Check the actual provider and arrangement

If you want to use an experience listed among the [resort facilities](/facilities), confirm availability, suitability, duration and any charge for your dates. Do not assume a leisure facility can accommodate a corporate activity in the format you imagine.

For specialist activities, agree the provider, facilitation and operating arrangements. Describe the participant group and ask the responsible professionals to confirm what is appropriate. Keep the scope in the written proposal.
Leave time for a useful debrief
An activity becomes more relevant when participants can connect it to how they work. Ask what they noticed, what helped the group and what they would do differently.
Keep the discussion specific and avoid turning a light session into an assessment of individual employees. The objective is shared learning or connection, not a surprise performance review.
Put the activity in the right place
An energetic or lengthy programme immediately before a difficult decision session may not fit the agenda. A late arrival can also leave little appetite for an organised evening.
Use the [two-day offsite agenda](/blogs/two-day-corporate-offsite-agenda-corbett) to identify a sensible slot. Check how the activity affects meals, venue changeovers and departure plans.

Discuss the complete programme through the [corporate offsite page](/corporate-offsites), and include the confirmed arrangement in the [budget](/blogs/corporate-offsite-budget-corbett). A successful activity earns its place by supporting the group, not by filling an empty hour.

title: A Conference Setup Checklist for Your Corbett Offsite
seoTitle: Corbett Conference Setup Checklist | Meeting Planning
description: Prepare your Corbett meeting brief with room layout, presentation needs, connectivity, working groups, technical checks and clear setup responsibilities.

blocks.text: A meeting space needs to be planned around the work taking place inside it. A presentation, a workshop and a small-group discussion can require different layouts, equipment and support. Start with the session format instead of asking only how many people fit in the hall.

Corbett The Grand lists conference facilities among its resort experiences. Discuss the actual space, setup and services available for your dates through the [corporate offsite enquiry](/corporate-offsites).
Define the room arrangement
Explain the participant count, presentation style and how people need to interact. Ask the venue team to review the proposed layout after equipment, circulation and service needs are included.

blocks.caption: Define the room arrangement
rows: Can everyone see and hear the material?
Is there suitable working space for participants?
Can people converse without constantly moving furniture?
What technical requirements must be met?
Which separate areas are actually available?

blocks.text: Do not treat a published or discussed capacity as confirmation that every layout will work for the same number of people.
Specify equipment by task

Describe what presenters will do: show slides, play media, write ideas, join a remote speaker or work on shared documents. Ask which equipment is included and which items require separate arrangement.

Confirm connections, microphones, display requirements and technical support. Keep a list of the equipment you are bringing and any compatibility questions. The person delivering the session should review the requirements, not only the person approving the room booking.
Verify connectivity requirements explicitly
If the programme depends on online access, discuss the actual load and importance of that access. Multiple video calls or large uploads require a different conversation from occasional email.

Ask the team about the available arrangement and limitations for the meeting space. Prepare suitable offline material where possible and do not promise participants a speed or uninterrupted service that has not been established.
Plan a setup and testing period

Agree when the team can access the space, who will be present and what needs to be checked. A rehearsal or equipment check should happen before participants are waiting for the first session to begin.

items: Check the material on the actual display.
Review sound and microphone use.
Confirm seating and visibility.
Establish the technical contact.
Check the break and catering arrangement.
Identify how the room will change between sessions.

blocks.text: These checks should be proportionate to the programme. The point is to resolve essential dependencies before the meeting starts.
Keep responsibility clear
Name the meeting owner, facilitator, venue contact and person approving additional services. Share a concise running order and identify the most recent version.

Use the [offsite agenda guide](/blogs/two-day-corporate-offsite-agenda-corbett) to connect the setup with the programme and the [budget guide](/blogs/corporate-offsite-budget-corbett) to record inclusions. A comfortable room supports the meeting, but a clear technical and operating brief makes it much more likely that the work can proceed as intended.

title: Organising Travel and Rooming for a Company Offsite in Corbett
seoTitle: Corbett Company Offsite Travel and Rooming Guide
description: Coordinate a company Corbett trip with accurate room requirements, arrival manifests, participant communication and a realistic meeting start.

blocks.text: Group travel affects the offsite before the first session begins. Participants may arrive from different offices, have different room requirements and need to leave on different services. A useful logistics plan turns those differences into a manageable arrival and departure process.
Choose one coordinator for the working rooming and transport information. Keep the data needed for booking separate from the simple itinerary sent to all participants.
Establish the rooming approach first

Ask the organisation to decide its rooming requirements before requesting a final quotation. Do not assume colleagues will share, that twin beds are available or that every room category supports the same arrangement.

Discuss the actual [accommodation options](/accommodation) with the venue. Record the confirmed approach and identify any specific access requirement through an appropriate private channel. Room preferences and personal information should not become an open group discussion.
Build an arrival manifest
Use the actual transport arrangements rather than one assumed arrival time for the whole company. Record the person responsible for each group and how changes will be communicated.

blocks.caption: Build an arrival manifest
rows: Prevents the return journey being forgotten

blocks.text: Agree who updates the list. Multiple independent versions can lead to a car being arranged twice or a late participant being missed.
Set a realistic meeting start
Work backwards from arrival, luggage, room access and the first meal. A programme should not begin on the assumption that every traveller reaches the property exactly on time.

If the first discussion is essential for everyone, allow a suitable arrival window or consider whether the previous night is needed. Use the [two-day agenda](/blogs/two-day-corporate-offsite-agenda-corbett) to place the important work after the group is ready to participate.
Send participants a short practical note

Include the property name, location, travel arrangement, first meeting time and the person handling changes. Explain what participants need to bring for sessions and whether any optional activity has specific requirements.

Use the [how to reach page](/how-to-reach) for Corbett The Grand's location. Separate the resort journey from any safari or other excursion. An offsite transport booking does not automatically cover every outing someone may want to take.
Reconcile changes before departure
Check the final rooming list, meal count and return manifest together. Someone leaving early may affect a meal and a vehicle but not necessarily the agreed accommodation charges.
Confirm the procedure for added nights, extra services and participant substitutions within the actual booking conditions. Keep one authorised contact for changes that affect cost.

Discuss the complete requirements on the [corporate offsite page](/corporate-offsites) and use the [budget guide](/blogs/corporate-offsite-budget-corbett) to keep the assumptions consistent. Good logistics make it easier for the team to focus on the reason it travelled.

title: How to Measure Whether Your Corbett Corporate Offsite Worked
seoTitle: Measure Corporate Offsite Success | Corbett Planning Guide
description: Define useful offsite outcomes, record decisions and review follow-through after your Corbett company gathering instead of measuring success only by attendance.

blocks.text: A successful offsite should leave the organisation with something more useful than photographs and a completed attendance list. That might be a decision, a working plan, a stronger shared understanding or a set of actions people actually carry out. Decide what success means before the team travels.
Corbett provides a setting away from the usual office routine, but the location cannot supply the business outcome by itself. The agenda, facilitation and follow-up need to do that work.
Define one primary outcome

Write a statement that can be reviewed later. Compare a vague objective such as build alignment with a more specific one: agree three priorities, name an owner for each and schedule a progress review.

Keep the objective proportionate to the time available. An overnight meeting cannot reasonably solve every organisational issue. Use the [two-day agenda guide](/blogs/two-day-corporate-offsite-agenda-corbett) to connect the sessions to the decision you need.
Gather a starting point
Before the event, ask participants what is unclear, what is blocking progress or what decision they need from the group. Keep the questions short and relevant.

This provides context for the facilitator and helps prevent the programme being driven entirely by the loudest voices on the day. Use an appropriate process for confidential feedback rather than putting personal comments in a public event document.
Record outputs while the group is together
Assign someone to capture decisions, unresolved questions and next actions. A long transcript is less useful than a clear record of what was agreed.

blocks.caption: Record outputs while the group is together
rows: The agreed choice and its scope
What must happen before work can proceed
Progress at the agreed review point

blocks.text: These measures are examples. Choose those that fit the actual purpose of your offsite rather than collecting data simply because it is easy to count.
Review the participant experience separately
Ask whether the schedule, room setup, breaks, travel and activities supported the work. This feedback can improve the next programme even when the main business outcome was achieved.

Use the [conference setup checklist](/blogs/conference-setup-checklist-corbett) and [travel planning guide](/blogs/company-offsite-travel-rooming-corbett) to identify practical improvements. Avoid confusing satisfaction with the venue and completion of the business objective; both matter, but they answer different questions.
Follow up on the date you promised
Send the concise decision record and hold the agreed review. Check progress against the actions rather than relying on people's memory of the event.

Compare actual spending with the [approved budget](/blogs/corporate-offsite-budget-corbett) and record material changes in scope. A cost-per-participant calculation can describe spending efficiency, but it does not by itself show whether a useful decision was implemented.

When planning [a corporate offsite at Corbett The Grand](/corporate-offsites), share both the participant requirements and the intended programme. The most valuable result is a gathering whose decisions survive the journey back to work.
